listing.name: LTV_Economy | An economy overhaul with population mechanics
listing.summary: Overhauls the economy with unit-based production, worker management, and population mechanics.

description:
Before the fleets meet, before the first blow lands, another battle's finished by unseen hands. In mines. In factories. Across a thousand worlds and strands.

Spoiler

[close]

A deep overhaul of Starsector's economy and additional colony systems.

LTV-Economy replaces abstract production values with a

unit-based simulation

where production and trade correspond to actual cargo units.

The mod deepens economic simulation by introducing

workers

as a production factor. Player-enacted policies and market events build on top of this framework.

Trade and patrol fleets are deeply integrated into the economy, corresponding to concrete trade missions, and assembled from the faction ship inventory.

Features

Industries consume and produce in cargo units equivalent to a tonThe output of industries are determined by the workers assigned to them.Population simulation (health, happiness, cohesion) and corresponding effects on the colonyCustom faction management options related to the economyPeer-to-Peer market trade logicExpanded colony UI and new management panelsFaction ship inventory used for creating trade and patrol fleets

Requirements

WrapUI (download)

Recommended Mods

LunaLib (Mod configuration in-game)

Compatibility

Cannot be added mid-saveCannot be removed mid-saveThe changelogs specify if the latest release was compatible with the previous one

Incompatible Mods

Grand.Colonies (Built-in scrollbar makes it redundant)Astral Ascension (technically works but numbers get ridiculous)Ashes of The Domain (has its own economic overhaul)Starpocalypse Revengeance (overrides submarkets)

QnA

Spoiler

Why did you make this mod?
Even though I knew the game was a combat simulator, I still felt the need to make the economy more alive. The way scale was represented in vanilla never sat right with me. Trade fleets were completely disconnected from actual goods. I based the rework on a simple economic theory and started reworking systems one by one. Production, trade, and finally fleets. Now I have inner peace, the economy of the game feels more real to me.
Why did you introduce new population mechanics?
Not being able to meaningfully interact with the population of my colonies always left a sour taste. I wanted to give the colonies more depth. Make them feel more alive.
What content does this mod add?
Nothing. This mod is not supposed to be a main attraction like a faction mod. It is supposed to run in the background and permanently change how colonies and the player faction is managed in general. However, it does have some flavor bar events.
Any vanilla mechanics not supported by the mod?
There are two that come to mind. Supply contracts and colony crises. I don't feel like re-creating the supply contract mission you can encounter in bars. As for the colony crises, I don't want to re-create the vanilla crises just so that they are compatible with my mod. Further, modded crises would also need to be modified in that case. Thus, both systems use the vanilla economy, which is hidden, but still running.
Why workers?
Three reasons. Firstly, one of the first problems encountered when making production more realistic is determining how much an industry is supposed to produce. I didn't want to come up with arbitrary values, so I decided to give myself a "tuning knob" if you will, to control industry outputs. The workers also answered the scale question. If the value produced by a worker is constant, and a constant portion of the value of industrial outputs come from
workers, then we have an equation to know exactly how much an industry produces. The equation is supplied by LTV in this case.

Secondly, I didn't like the vanilla premise that a built industry is a fully functional one. This let the player have a mega-colony with twenty different industries (thanks to Grand-Colonies) producing absolutely everything. I wanted a way to make this more realistic. One can have twenty different industries. But the pool of workers to operate said industries are limited. This prevents the player from playing absurdly tall.

Thirdly, the non-abstract input and output values of industries meant that there was a specific amount of commodities the sector demanded each day, measured in cargo units. Having workers as tuning knobs allowed me to assign NPC colony workers in a way that would lead to sector-wide demand fulfillment.
Is this a feature overhaul mod?
In the general sense, yes. This mod overhauls the vanilla economy, replaces trade fleets and patrol fleets. But there is a small nuance. The mod does not actually touch the vanilla economy, which still runs in the background. LTV-Economy runs separately on the side. The vanilla user interface is simply modified to use the data from ltv economy. The aim with this approach is ensuring high compatibility with other mods without dedicated patches.
What is the Compatibility scope of this mod?
I aim to make the mod compatible with most mods out there. There are some necessary exceptions. AoTD has its own economic overhaul. Starpocalypse replaces some vanilla stuff that my mod also replaces. Grand.Colonies is integrated into the mod etc. But if a mod not present inside the "Incompatible Mods" causes a crash when alongside my mod, then please report it so that I can fix it.
I cannot bother managing worker allocations for all my colonies.
This becomes a hassle especially when there are multiple colonies who produce just enough to feed each other, but then one colony grows in size and throws the production chain off-balance. Luckily there is a tool for that. Command -> Faction -> Administration -> Workforce Planner. Then all you have to do is select either one of the presets or create your own plan and run it.
I cannot bother selecting what ships to produce for my faction hangar.
There is a tool for that. Command -> Faction -> Administration -> Auto-manage ship construction to meet trade demands
My colonies are in so much debt, what do I do?
No need to panic. Debt only causes stability, upkeep and growth maluses. Here is a checklist: 
Try to reduce unnecessary imports. This could mean downgrading the ground defenses, removing that space station or not getting a patrolHQ on all of your colonies.Avoid trade as much as possible. Fleets cost money, fuel costs money and buying from a foreign faction that wants to make a profit costs money as well. Try to produce locally what your colony demands. Try in-faction production if that is not possible.Keep your colonies close to each other, and keep your faction close to the core worlds. Since fuel costs for trade fleets scale with distance.Control the size of your faction hangar. You don't need 100 onslaughts to haul cargo. Pick cargo efficient ships if you are struggling with trade capacity.Independent captains love to haul your cheap food and ore. They get paid per-ton and per commodity value. For cheap goods, the money you pay them can sometimes exceed your export profits. Avoid exporting cheap goods using independent captains, i.e. expand your faction hangar.Create in-faction production chains. They are cheaper and more efficient.Track your finances. The detailed income breakdown menu is there for a reason.I stole the Synchrotron Core of Sindria and the entire sector ran out of fuel!
Don't bite the hand that feeds you.

changelog.0.98: Initial release of LTV-Economy with core systems: unit-based production, worker management, population simulation, and integrated trade/patrol fleets.
